title: Development of Mobile (Quadruped)/Handheld Device/System for Real-Time Detection of Narcotics and Explosives across Indian Railways.
description:
Background:
Indian Railways is one of the largest rail networks in the world, serving millions of passengers daily across thousands of stations, platforms, and train coaches. Ensuring the safety and security of passengers and railway assets is a critical responsibility of the Railway Protection Force (RPF).Drug trafficking through railway networks and threats arising from explosives and Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs) have emerged as major security concerns. During the year 2025, RPF recovered narcotic substances worth approximately Rs. 300 Crores in more than 2100 instances.However, as per data of Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB), nearly 15-20% of drug trafficking is routed through the railway network. Similarly, recent incidents involving use of high explosives such as RDX on railway tracks highlight the vulnerability of railway infrastructure to hostile activities.At present, Indian Railways does not possess any dedicated mobile quadruped or handheld system for real-time field detection of narcotics and explosives. This severely limits the capability of RPF personnel to conduct rapid, non-intrusive screening at station entry points, platforms, inside train coaches, and during luggage or parcel screening operations. Therefore, there is an urgent requirement for a modern, technology-driven, ruggedised, and easy-to-operate detection system suitable for Indian Railways operational conditions.
Description:
The proposed problem statement envisages development of an AI-enabled Mobile (Quadruped) Device/System and Handheld Device/System for real-time detection of narcotics and explosives across Indian Railways.The Mobile (Quadruped) Device/System should function as an intelligent robotic surveillance platform capable of operating in hazardous, complex, and GPS-denied environments. The system should support autonomous or semi-autonomous navigation using LiDAR-based mapping, sensor fusion, thermal and optical imaging systems, and real-time video surveillance. It should be capable of operating in dusty, humid, high-temperature, low-light, and uneven railway environments including ballast areas, yards, tunnels, platforms, and coaches.The quadruped system should support underframe inspection of coaches/wagons, yard surveillance, night patrolling, bomb detection assistance, narcotics detection, facial recognition and matching, and inspection of luggage and concealed areas inside train coaches. The system should also support secure wireless communication, onboard data logging, real-time transmission to control centres, obstacle detection and avoidance, fail-safe mechanisms, and long-duration deployment capability.The Handheld Device/System should be lightweight, ruggedised, easy to operate, and deployable by RPF personnel with minimal training. It should support offline and online operation, encrypted data storage, real-time alerts, GPS tagging, automatic event logging, multilingual interface, and integration with centralized monitoring systems. The device should enable non-intrusive screening crowded railway environments and support wireless transmission of alerts and threat information to control rooms or designated supervisors. Both systems should be capable of detecting a broad spectrum of narcotics including heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, cannabis derivatives, opium derivatives, semi-synthetic and synthetic narcotics, as well as explosives including RDX, TNT, PETN, TATP, C4, dynamite, ammonium nitrate compounds, gunpowder, and pyrotechnics.
Expected Solution:
A cost-effective, ruggedised, Al-enabled Mobile (Quadruped) Device/System and Handheld Device/System should be developed for real-time detection of narcotics and explosives across Indian Railways.The proposed solution should support rapid, non-intrusive, and real-time detection capability at railway stations, platforms, train coaches, luggage screening points, yards, and other vulnerable railway locations. The system should provide automated alerts through sound, visual indicators, vibration, and centralized monitoring dashboards along with timestamp and GPS-based event logging.The quadruped system should support autonomous patrolling, under-carriage inspection, thermal imaging, facial recognition, bomb detection support, and surveillance operations in hazardous or inaccessible areas. The handheld system should support quick deployment, easy usability, offline data storage, synchronization after network restoration, multilingual operation, and integration with Railway security infrastructure. The overall solution should be operationally sustainable, low-maintenance, scalable for largescale deployment, and suitable for continuous deployment under diverse Indian Railways operational and climatic conditions.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, autonomous, sensor fusion applied to a robotics and drones problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Robotics and Drones. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on integration, sensor, real-time. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: Development of Mobile (Quadruped)/Handheld Device/System for Real-Time Detection of Narcotics and Explosives across Indian Railways

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a portable or robotic detection system that RPF officers can use to quickly and safely screen for drugs and explosives at stations, on platforms, and inside train coaches, without disrupting passenger flow.
overview.why_it_matters: Indian Railways currently has no dedicated field detection capability for this, at the scale of Rs. 300 crores in narcotics recovered and real explosive threats, that's a serious operational gap.
pain_points: No dedicated mobile/handheld system for real-time narcotics or explosives screening exists on Indian Railways today.
RPF personnel lack rapid, non-intrusive screening tools at high-traffic points.
Manual screening doesn't scale to the volume of passengers and luggage across the network.
overview.background: Indian Railways faces significant narcotics trafficking and explosive threats through its network, but RPF currently has no dedicated field detection technology for rapid screening.
overview.whats_being_asked: A mobile (quadruped robot) or handheld detection system for real-time field screening of narcotics and explosives at stations, platforms, and inside train coaches.
expected_solution: Real-time detection capability for narcotics and explosives.
Mobile or handheld form factor usable by RPF field personnel.
Non-intrusive screening suitable for high-traffic environments.
Deployable at station entry points, platforms, and coach interiors.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. This requires real chemical/explosive detection sensing technology (not achievable via software alone), a genuinely hard hardware-sensing challenge with serious safety implications.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Very high. Real narcotics/explosives detection needs specialized sensors (ion mobility spectrometry, trace detection, etc.) that are not accessible hobbyist-grade hardware, this is a fundamentally different difficulty tier than most PS in this batch.

competitive_landscape.note: Extremely specialized security-hardware PS, very few teams will have any path to real sensing hardware, low competition but an exceptionally high skill/resource floor.

innovation.note: Real narcotics/explosives sensing is genuinely cutting-edge security technology, not something replicable with hackathon-accessible components.

invention.note: This is closer to defense/security R&D than a hackathon build, specialized sensor hardware isn't something a team can source or build in 36 hours.

technical_feasibility.note: There is no accessible, safe, legal way to test real narcotics or explosives detection at a hackathon venue, this is a hard constraint, not a scoping choice.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuinely critical security impact if solved, the stated statistics (Rs. 300 crores recovered, 15-20% trafficking share) underline the real stakes.

architecture.note: Real deployment would need certified detection hardware integrated with a mobile/robotic platform, well beyond typical hackathon scope.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red. This is one of the hardest PS in the entire batch to attempt meaningfully, real narcotics/explosives detection requires specialized, often export-controlled sensor technology that simply isn't accessible to a hackathon team. Only pick this if your team plans to build a software/logistics layer (e.g. deployment routing, data management for detection results) around assumed/simulated detection hardware, not the detection itself.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Extremely well-documented, high-stakes real-world need, the statistics cited make the impact case undeniable.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting to build or simulate 'real' narcotics/explosives detection is not achievable, and claiming to have solved it would be both technically dishonest and a red flag to any judge with security-domain knowledge.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: If attempting this PS at all, explicitly reframe your scope to the deployment/data/logistics layer around a detection system (e.g. how alerts get routed, how RPF coordinates a response), not the sensing technology itself, and state that reframing openly.

idea_0_4: Reframe the scope explicitly: you are not building real detection hardware, you're building the deployment, alerting, and coordination system around an assumed detection capability.
Decide on a clearly-labeled simulated detection input (e.g. a mock sensor API returning simulated alerts) to build around.
Split: one person on the mobile/handheld device interface concept, one on the alert-routing/coordination backend.
prototype_4_22: Build a simulated detection event generator, clearly framed as a stand-in for real sensor hardware.
Build the RPF-facing alert interface, handheld or mobile UI showing a detection event and recommended response.
Build the coordination/routing logic, how an alert gets escalated to the right response team.
integration_22_30: Connect the simulated detection trigger to the full alert-and-response flow.
Test with multiple simultaneous simulated events to show coordination logic handling load.
Add basic logging/audit trail for detection events, this matters for a security-context system.
polish_30_36: Polish the RPF-facing interface for field usability, clear, fast, low-cognitive-load under pressure.
Rehearse being completely upfront that the detection hardware itself is out of scope and simulated, explain why honestly.
Prepare to discuss what real deployment would require, partnership with defense/security tech providers.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Don't pretend to have solved detection. Lead with the honest reframe, 'here's the system that makes real detection hardware actually usable and coordinated in the field', that intellectual honesty will read far better than an implausible claim.

strengths: Extremely high-stakes, well-documented real-world need makes the impact case compelling if approached honestly.
Low competition, since most teams will avoid or misjudge this PS.
weaknesses: Core detection technology is genuinely inaccessible to a hackathon team, not a scoping problem, a hard constraint.
High risk of appearing to overclaim if the reframing isn't communicated clearly and immediately.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: No specialized hardware role needed if you correctly reframe scope, this becomes a systems/UX problem, not a sensing problem.
team_fit.approach: Agree on the honest reframe explicitly as a team before building anything, this PS punishes teams that don't confront the hardware reality upfront.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The alert interface and coordination/routing backend, both standard patterns once you've accepted the reframed scope.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Deciding how to honestly and clearly communicate the scope limitation to judges without undermining the pitch, that's a framing and communication judgment call, not a technical one.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Using AI tooling to generate confident-sounding claims about 'detection accuracy' for a system with no real sensing hardware would be actively misleading, this is a case where restraint matters more than output.

data_resource_availability.status: No accessible narcotics/explosives detection dataset or hardware exists for hackathon use, this is a fundamental, not sourcing-related, constraint.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: There is no meaningful backup for the detection technology itself, the only viable path is reframing to the surrounding deployment/coordination system, as described above.

judge_qna.question: Does your system actually detect narcotics or explosives?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be completely direct: no, real detection requires specialized, often export-controlled sensor hardware not accessible to a hackathon team, what we built is the field deployment and coordination system that would sit around such hardware in a real solution.
judge_qna.follow_up: What detection hardware exists in the real world that this could integrate with?

judge_qna.question: Isn't this just avoiding the actual hard part of the problem?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Acknowledge it directly, yes, the sensing technology is the hardest part and genuinely outside hackathon scope, we focused on the part that's both achievable and still adds real value: making any detection capability actually usable and coordinated in the field.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would your system change if plugged into an actual certified detection sensor?
